comparisons.peer_summary: VCF delivers integrated enterprise-class compute, networking, storage, management, and security across any environment, including native Kubernetes for VMs and containers, advanced AI/ML workloads support, and integrated data services.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Broadcom provide integrated, enterprise-class compute solutions that emphasize security, manageability, and AI capabilities, though they operate at different layers of the stack. AMD focuses on client-side commercial CPUs (Ryzen PRO) for business notebooks and workstations, offering enterprise-class security and manageability features. In contrast, Broadcom’s VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) provides integrated compute, networking, storage, and security for broader enterprise environments, including native Kubernetes and advanced AI/ML workloads at scale. While both target the commercial/enterprise sector with integrated security and AI, AMD’s disclosure is specific to client PC processors, whereas Broadcom’s is focused on cloud infrastructure and virtualization platforms.

sentences.text: The AMD PRO solutions include mobile laptops, desktops and workstations for large enterprise, mid-market and the small and medium business (SMB) customers.

We launched our AMD Ryzen AI PRO 300 series, bringing world-class security and manageability and leadership productivity, battery life, and AI capabilities to business notebooks and mobile workstations.

• VCF: VCF delivers integrated, enterprise-class compute, networking, storage, management, and security across any environment. VCF includes native Kubernetes to support both virtual machines and containerized workloads on a single platform, enables advanced AI and machine learning workloads at enterprise scale and offers integrated data services capabilities. Our solutions enhance our customers' ability to continuously optimize performance and costs, protect the business from threats and enable the business to focus on outcomes instead of operations through advanced observability and insights.

comparisons.peer_topic: Client CPU product launches and performance
comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, Intel launched Intel Core Ultra Series 1 (first with integrated NPU for AI workloads) and the power-efficient Intel Core Ultra 200V Series. Additionally, the 13th and 14th Gen Intel Core processors continued to serve a significant majority of client sales.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Intel actively compete in the commercial and consumer client PC CPU market, with both companies highlighting the launch of new processors featuring integrated AI capabilities (NPUs) in 2024. AMD launched the Ryzen AI PRO 300 series and Ryzen PRO 200 Series to address business notebooks and various price points, emphasizing productivity and AI capabilities. Similarly, Intel launched the Intel Core Ultra Series 1, its first product with an integrated neural processing unit (NPU), and the Intel Core Ultra 200V Series to showcase power efficiency and AI acceleration in thin and light notebooks. Both disclosures underscore a strategic shift towards 'AI PCs' driven by integrated neural processing units for local AI workloads.

sentences.text: We launched our AMD Ryzen AI PRO 300 series, bringing world-class security and manageability and leadership productivity, battery life, and AI capabilities to business notebooks and mobile workstations.

Our commitment to high performance leadership continued with the launch of AMD Ryzen PRO 200 Series mobile processors that expand our commercial CPU portfolio to enable PCs spanning a range of price points.

▪Client CPUs. In 2024, we ramped sales of the Intel® Core™ Ultra Series 1, our first product with an integrated neural processing unit for efficient processing of AI workload. The Intel Core Ultra Series 1, manufactured on the Intel 4 process, introduced the first AI PCs to the market. We also launched the Intel Core Ultra 200V Series, showcasing power efficiency and long-lasting battery life. The 200V Series, manufactured by an external foundry, leverages our Xe2 GPU architecture, bringing improved efficiency, second-generation ray tracing units and XMX AI acceleration to thin and light notebooks. During 2024, a significant majority of our client sales consisted of our 13th and 14th Gen Intel Core processors, manufactured on Intel 7, which allow us to serve the breadth of customer and computing needs in the client market.

comparisons.peer_topic: PC Market AI Capabilities and Client SSD Portfolio Expansion
comparisons.peer_summary: Next-generation PCs require higher performance SSDs due to AI capabilities; SBU expanded its portfolio in 2024 with the 3500 NVMe SSD built on Micron G8 NAND, targeting demanding business and consumer workloads.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Micron address the evolving demands of the next-generation PC market driven by AI capabilities. AMD’s disclosure focuses on providing the compute engines (CPUs like Ryzen PRO and Threadripper PRO) that enable these AI capabilities in commercial client devices. Micron’s disclosure complements this by describing the storage requirements for these 'next generation PCs,' noting that AI capabilities require higher performance and capacity SSDs. While AMD provides the processing solutions for the AI PC, Micron provides the high-performance storage solutions (like the 3500 NVMe SSD) needed to support the demanding workloads of business applications and AI on those devices.

comparisons.peer_summary: Beyond integral platform software, the company offers paid licenses for NVIDIA AI Enterprise, an enterprise-grade AI software suite, and NVIDIA vGPU software for graphics-rich virtual desktops and workstations.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and NVIDIA provide software and hardware solutions for enterprise AI and virtual desktops, targeting similar commercial workloads. AMD highlights its AMD PRO solutions for commercial client PCs, emphasizing enterprise-class security and manageability, and mentions AI capabilities in its Ryzen AI PRO processors. NVIDIA offers NVIDIA AI Enterprise, a comprehensive suite of enterprise-grade AI software, and NVIDIA vGPU software for graphics-rich virtual desktops and workstations. While AMD focuses on the CPU-based client security and AI processing, NVIDIA focuses on the AI software stack and virtualized GPU resources for workstations, representing complementary or overlapping strategies in the enterprise AI workspace.

sentences.text: Our AMD PRO technology solution offers enterprise-class security features manageability, reliability and extended image stability, for commercial client PCs.
The AMD Ryzen PRO 8000G series desktops offer an integrated AI desktop solution for enterprises, and our AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO CPU enables leadership performance for premium workstations.

In addition to software delivered to customers as an integral part of our data center computing platform, we offer paid licenses to NVIDIA AI Enterprise, a comprehensive suite of enterprise-grade AI software and NVIDIA vGPU software for graphics-rich virtual desktops and workstations.

comparisons.peer_summary: Consumer IoT products are adopting latest mobile connectivity and on-device AI capabilities, with new AI-focused PCs launching in 2024 and analysts expecting 50% of PCs sold to be AI capable by 2027.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Qualcomm are driving the adoption of AI-enabled personal computers, with both companies launching or supplying components for AI-focused PCs in 2024. AMD launched the Ryzen AI PRO 300 series for business notebooks, integrating AI capabilities for productivity. Qualcomm supplied the Snapdragon X Series platforms for a new class of AI-focused PCs that launched in 2024, enabling on-device AI processing at low power. Both disclosures reflect the industry-wide transition to 'AI PCs' with on-device intelligence, though AMD focuses on x86 commercial CPUs and Qualcomm focuses on Snapdragon-based architectures.
